featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Can we talk about a Biryani that survives a flight and still tastes like it was just served? ✈️

I recently tried this all the way from Mumbai to Bengaluru, and I am blown away. Even after the journey, the packaging was perfectly intact and so neat. All it took was a quick minute in the microwave, and it was ready to eat!

What really stands out is the quality. You can tell this is premium, the aroma of pure ghee and saffron is so rich and authentic. Usually, in veg biryanis, the veggies can feel bland, but here, every piece of cauliflower, aloo, and bean is packed with masala. It’s flavour in every single bite! 😋

Also, a huge shoutout for the eco-friendly packaging. It’s so inspiring to see a brand prioritize the planet without compromising on the experience. Even the papad stayed perfectly crispy, and the onions were fresh. I loved it, and now I’m just waiting for them to open an outlet in Bangalore! 📍✨

Sharing good food is a love language, so if you’re in Mumbai (or traveling from there), you have to try this. I’m definitely ordering this for my friends!

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Anita Kapai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Butter Chicken Factory in Bandra is a haven for butter chicken enthusiasts. The restaurant's rendition of this classic dish is a delightful symphony of flavors – the chicken is perfectly marinated, the creamy tomato-based gravy strikes a harmonious balance of spice and sweetness. Each bite is a journey for the senses, a true culinary delight.

Sujeet's service adds a personal touch to the dining experience, ensuring a memorable visit. The mocktails, especially Pudeena Pani and Masala Shikanje, provide a refreshing start to the meal.

The Kabab Platter showcases a variety of both vegetarian and non-vegetarian delights. From the succulent Paneer Tikka to the flavorful Chicken Seekh Kebab, the assortment caters to diverse preferences.

Moving on to the mains, the Butter Chicken steals the show with its rich and decadent texture. Complemented by Butter Paneer and Dal Makhani, the restaurant offers a fulfilling array of choices.

The Bread Basket, featuring Chilli Garlic Laccha Paratha, Tandoori Roti, Pudina Paratha, and Churchur Naan, provides the perfect accompaniment to soak up the flavorful gravies. Rice lovers are not forgotten, as the restaurant offers a satisfying selection.

The meal concludes on a sweet note with Gulab Jamun, leaving diners with a lingering sweetness that perfectly caps off the gastronomic journey. Butter Chicken Factory in Bandra is undeniably a go-to spot for those seeking an authentic and indulgent butter chicken experience in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Rohan Bidi
featured_reviews.review_text: It's quite small, only a few tables, so coming in a large group isn't a good idea. For starters we ordered Dahi Ke Kebab and Kaali Mirch Chicken Tikka. The kebabs were okay, didn't quite have a specific flavour, though their taste was enhanced a lot by the accompanying chutney and spiced onions. The tikka was quite tender, would've liked the kaali mirch flavour to be a little stronger, but wasn't a bad dish at all. Along with the starters we had Lemon Iced Tea, and I liked it a lot, being served chilled and not diluted. And now we come to the business end of the meal, for this is what makes this place so good, the main course. Our order was Butter Chicken, Soya Tikka Masala, Chur Naan, Garlic Naan and Hari Mirch Lachha Paratha. And boy was all of it good!! I particularly liked the soya tikka and the paratha, and the Chur Naan was interesting too. The Garlic Naan complimented the soya tikka perfectly, and we ended up having a very satisfying lunch, more than happy to have visited this place. To sum it up, I highly recommend Butter Chicken Factory, tiny but comfy, very tasty main course, polite staff, worth visiting more than just once.

The food was definitely the highlight, super tasty 😋. Honestly didn’t expect the veg(Paneer & Mashroom) options to be this good, but we absolutely loved them. The veg starters were amazing and easily one of the best parts of the meal.

The Chicken Tikka Biryani is a must try, highly recommended ❤️. Also you could try chicken lollipop and chilli chicken dry😋.

featured_reviews.name: Jasmine Salvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️ (3/5)
Visited Taste of Hyderabad, Powai for lunch.
The food taste is good, though slightly on the spicier side. The mutton rogan josh deserves a mention — fresh, tender mutton and properly cooked. No complaints about the food quality.
However, the service was absolutely PATHETIC, DISRESPECTFUL, and MANNERLESS.
Only one staff member behaved politely and served us well. The rest were extremely rude and unprofessional.
One waiter snatched the menu while my mobile was kept on it, moving my phone aside without permission.
Another waiter was asked to change plates and refused, saying “these are clean,” without even checking.
A third waiter spoke loudly and rudely, saying “acha order dena hai aapko abhi” — completely unacceptable tone and attitude.
Good food alone cannot justify such poor hospitality. If the management doesn’t train staff on basic manners and customer respect, it ruins the entire dining experience.
Would only recommend if service standards improve drastically.
